method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, call target, vftable cell and type byte was compared with those listings. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts are call-site counts from xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json and counts of retail capture messages from the cited study. The descriptor strings are INFERRED from a local scan of the installed chunks that no tracked artifact carries. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of the PlayerBase command, talk, emote and push natives and the NpcBase server request natives: _executeCommand, _canExecuteCommand, _cancelCommand, _isCommandPlaying, _countCommandPlaying, _executeTalk, _canExecuteTalk, _cancelTalk, _executeEmote, _canExecuteEmote, _cancelEmote, _cancelNotice, _cancelPush, _isPushingOut, _callServerOnCommand, _doServerOnCommand, _callServerOnTalk, _callServerOnEmote, _callServerOnPush, _doServerOnTalk, _doServerOnEmote and _doServerOnPush. Each row gives the registration site, the dispatch to the MyPlayer routine or the NpcBase callback, the declared argument and return lists, the cell reads and gates, the effects on client state, the serverbound record where one is built, the yield behavior and the corpus call sites. Client-side contracts do not establish command names, condition names, server behavior or the effect of a dispatched entry.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact
tierVocabulary: STATIC: read directly from instructions or data at the cited addresses
MEASURED: counted or parsed by the method named in the fact
INFERRED: a name or role taken from the surrounding instructions or scripts that the bytes do not state

framework.playerBaseSplit: Every PlayerBase callback of this record is a thunk that jumps through a PlayerBase virtual slot. The PlayerBase cell of each slot is a bare ret 4, so only a MyPlayer receiver (vftable 0x00FD785C) reaches a routine and any other PlayerBase receiver pushes nothing.

eventState.sentinel: The dword at 0x0130C778 holds 0xE0000000 in the image. The command, talk and emote routines compare references with it. The reference default constructor 0x00CC9310 stores that dword into its object and the destructor 0x00CC9330 is a bare ret, so a reference local that no 0x00CC73B0 conversion replaces reads as the sentinel. 0x00894200 and 0x00894370 treat a queried reference equal to the sentinel as matching every entry reference.

player.+0x5C: Byte. A zero byte makes the can-execute natives and _isCommandPlaying push false.
player.+0xF8: Policy manager, the ECX of every dispatcher. Manager +0x08 is the current entry, +0x0C a staged entry, +0x10 and +0x14 a list head, +0x1E a byte read by 0x00893320.
player.+0x128: Dword compared with the sentinel and with the command actor reference.

npc.+0x5C: Byte. A zero byte rejects the receiver in the talk and emote routines.
npc.+0x5D: Byte. A nonzero byte rejects the receiver.

condition.+0x58: Byte compared with the byte at 0x012C3F77 by the scans.
condition.+0x5C: Word. In emote conditions 0x0FFF is a wildcard and any other value is an emote id.
condition.vftable slot 6 (+0x18): Compares a type byte address argument with the type byte.
condition.vftable slot 7 (+0x1C): Returns 1 for the blocking classes and 0 for the non-blocking classes.
condition.vftable slot 8 (+0x20): Writes a priority byte to its argument and returns the argument. The block classes read it from the object (CommandBlock +0x5C through 0x008999D0, EmoteBlock +0x60 through 0x00899350). Both non-block classes share 0x008993C0, which writes the run-time global byte at 0x01355296.

argumentConversion.intEntry: Registry entry 0 installs the inner vftable 0x0110DF38 at 0x00CC9DC9. Its +4 cell 0x0110DF3C holds 0x00CFAC40, the only vftable cell that references that address. For a Lua nil, which 0x00CF3760 tests, 0x00CFAC40 builds a Nil cell (tag 6) through 0x00583F70. Otherwise it reads the number through 0x00CF35C0 (0x00DCDED0, which yields 0.0 for a value that is neither a number nor a numeric string), converts it through 0x009D6600 and builds a tag 0 cell through 0x00583D90 from the 32-bit result. No range test sits between the conversion and the cell.
argumentConversion.conversion: 0x009D6600 tests the dword at 0x0137B8E8. A nonzero dword takes the cvttsd2si with a 32-bit destination at 0x009D6615, which yields 0x80000000 for a value outside the signed 32-bit range. A zero dword branches to 0x009D6636, the x87 64-bit truncation, and 0x00CFAC40 keeps its low dword. The dword lies in zero-filled virtual memory. The only direct writer found in .text is 0x009F6600, which stores the result of the feature test 0x009F659B, and that test reads bit 26 of CPUID leaf 1 EDX at 0x009F65DF and then calls the check 0x009F654B (not traced).
argumentConversion.consequence: On the cvttsd2si branch an integral Lua number outside the signed 32-bit range, for example 4294967295 or 1099511627776, reaches the cell as 0x80000000. This applies to the declared int arguments of this record and to the integral numbers of a Variable list, whose selector 0x00CF89B5 admits integral values within the signed 64-bit range (manifests/player_command_wire_contract.json luaBridge).
argumentConversion.tier: STATIC for the code and the cell. The run-time value of the dword at 0x0137B8E8 was not observed, so the branch a given host takes is unknown.

rows.callbackKind: thunk through a PlayerBase virtual slot

dispatch.thunk: mov eax,[ecx], mov eax,[eax+0xA8], jmp eax

arguments.note: Command name. An empty cell vector reaches 0x009D22B4 at 0x0070A0B6.
Command actor, read as an ActorBase. A null pointer passes the reader. An empty or one cell vector reaches 0x009D22B4 at 0x0070A0F7.
Cells from index 1 on are copied as a vector. The declared Variable collects the remaining Lua arguments, as luaBridge in manifests/player_command_wire_contract.json records.

returns.note: False on every gate failure. Otherwise the byte that the policy dispatcher 0x00898480 returns.

rows.behavior: Looks up the command descriptor by name in the vector at player +0xFC, resolves the command actor to a binding reference and applies three gates. The first gate applies while the dword at player +0x128 equals the dword at 0x0130C778. It then requires the dword at +0x12C to equal it too, a record under key 0 in the package tree and a zero byte at +0x1E of the policy manager. The second gate requires the reference of the command actor to equal the dword at player +0x128 unless that dword is the 0x0130C778 value. The third gate walks the copied cells and fails when a control argument is neither registry classified nor flagged live by the bytes at control +0x5C and +0x5D. A passing call hands the manager at player +0xF8 the descriptor, the reference and the copied cells through 0x00898480, which starts the blocking state machine 0x00897310 or the queue entry 0x00896510 by the descriptor virtual slot 7. It requests no yield. A PlayerBase receiver that is not a MyPlayer pushes nothing.

facts.claim: The thunk loads slot 0xA8. The PlayerBase cell 0x00FD5EAC is a bare ret 4 and the MyPlayer cell 0x00FD7904 holds 0x0070A010, slot 42 of the MyPlayer vftable 0x00FD785C.

The first gate branches on the dword at player +0x128. A value different from the dword at 0x0130C778 skips the rest of the gate. When it matches, a second dword at player +0x12C different from it pushes false. When both match, the callback looks up key 0 in the package tree at the manager that 0x006F51A0 returns and pushes false for an absent record. A present record is followed by a test of the byte at +0x1E of the object at player +0xF8, and only a zero byte continues.

The package key is the local that 0x0070A057 zeroes after its address is pushed. The tree search is the lower-bound lookup that the item package contract records for _hasItemPackage, so key 0 stands for package number 1 under that native's number-minus-1 rule.

The name is read from cell 0 and looked up with 0x0071CA50 on player +0xFC. The routine returns the first vector entry whose name equals the argument, or 0. No instruction tests the result before 0x00898480 calls its virtual slot 7, so the run-time result for an unknown name is unknown.
Cell 1 is converted to a binding reference through 0x00CC73B0 on ExecuteParameters +0x04. When player +0x128 is not the 0x0130C778 value and differs from that reference, the callback pushes false.

The copied cell vector is built by 0x00753B90 from index 1. For each tag 4 cell with a non-null control pointer the callback resolves a reference and calls the registry predicates 0x00CC7190 and 0x00CC70B0. When both answer false it requires the byte at control +0x5C to be nonzero and the byte at control +0x5D to be zero, and otherwise pushes false. A non-tag-4 cell is skipped.

The dispatch call passes the player, the descriptor, the reference and the copied vector with ECX set to player +0xF8. The returned byte is pushed through the bool pusher. The wire effect of the dispatch is outside the native.
The roles of the dword at player +0x128, the dword at +0x12C and the byte at manager +0x1E were not traced. The names event owner and blocked flag are not claimed.
